new.title: The Tenant's 14-Day Cure Notice When You Breach
new.bodyText: If you materially fail to comply with the lease, or fail to meet your maintenance duties under §76-1419 in a way that materially affects health and safety, the tenant may give you a written notice that describes the breach and says the lease will end on a date at least 30 days after you receive the notice if the breach is not remedied in fourteen days. If the breach can be remedied by repairs, by paying damages or otherwise, and you adequately remedy it before the date in the notice, the lease does not end. If substantially the same breach happens again within six months after such a notice, the tenant may end the lease on at least 14 days' written notice that names the breach and the termination date, with no new chance to cure. The tenant may not terminate for a condition the tenant, a family member or a guest caused deliberately or negligently. Separately, the tenant may recover damages and get an injunction for any breach of the lease or §76-1419, plus reasonable attorney's fees if your breach is willful; if the breach was caused by conditions beyond your control, the tenant cannot recover consequential damages but keeps the heat, water and essential-services remedies of §76-1427. A tenant who uses those essential-services remedies for a breach cannot also use this section for the same breach (§76-1427(2)). If the lease ends under this section, you must return the prepaid rent and security the tenant is entitled to under §76-1416 (§76-1425).
new.notes: NE: §76-1425 read whole (Laws 1974, LB 293, § 25; Laws 2001, LB 7, § 16), with §76-1427(2); the 14-day cure window was stated in no NE row: the tenant's notice states 'that the rental agreement will terminate upon a date not less than thirty days after receipt of the notice if the breach is not remedied in fourteen days'.

note: NE: §76-1425 read whole (Laws 1974, LB 293, § 25; Laws 2001, LB 7, § 16), with §76-1427(2); the 14-day cure window was stated in no NE row: the tenant's notice states 'that the rental agreement will terminate upon a date not less than thirty days after receipt of the notice if the breach is not remedied in fourteen days'.
quote: (1) ... the tenant may deliver a written notice to the landlord specifying the acts and omissions constituting the breach and that the rental agreement will terminate upon a date not less than thirty days after receipt of the notice if the breach is not remedied in fourteen days ... If substantially the same act or omission which constituted a prior noncompliance of which notice was given recurs within six months, the tenant may terminate the rental agreement upon at least fourteen days' written notice ... The tenant may not terminate for a condition caused by the deliberate or negligent act or omission of the tenant, a member of his or her family, or other person on the premises with his or her consent. (2) ... If the landlord's noncompliance is willful the tenant may recover reasonable attorney's fees. ... (4) If the rental agreement is terminated, the landlord shall return all prepaid rent and security recoverable by the tenant under section 76-1416.

new.title: Renting Out a Married Owner's Homestead
new.bodyText: If you are married and the property you are renting out is your homestead, Nebraska law says a married person's homestead 'cannot be conveyed or encumbered unless the instrument by which it is conveyed or encumbered is executed and acknowledged by both spouses' (§40-104). The statute does not say whether a lease is a conveyance or an encumbrance for this purpose. The cautious course is to have both spouses sign the lease, and for a long lease to have both signatures acknowledged before a notary. This does not apply to property that is not your homestead.
new.notes: NE: §40-104 read whole (Source ends Laws 2015, LB253, § 1): 'the homestead of a married person cannot be conveyed or encumbered unless the instrument by which it is conveyed or encumbered is executed and acknowledged by both spouses'; the text does not say whether a lease is an encumbrance, so the row states the cautious course rather than resting on case law.

note: NE: §40-104 read whole (Source ends Laws 2015, LB253, § 1): 'the homestead of a married person cannot be conveyed or encumbered unless the instrument by which it is conveyed or encumbered is executed and acknowledged by both spouses'; the text does not say whether a lease is an encumbrance, so the row states the cautious course rather than resting on case law.
quote: Except as otherwise provided in this section, the homestead of a married person cannot be conveyed or encumbered unless the instrument by which it is conveyed or encumbered is executed and acknowledged by both spouses.

new.title: When a City Declares the Property Unfit
new.bodyText: When a Nebraska city or village decides that a property is unsafe or unfit for human occupancy because it violates the local minimum standard housing ordinance, or that a building is unsafe under the local building code, the city must post the property and record its decision with the county register of deeds (§18-1722.01). The decision therefore shows on the property's public record, and the posting tells your tenants. If a tenant is removed by a government order because the property is unfit to live in due to your negligence or neglect, the tenant is not liable for damages directly related to that removal (§76-1416(4)).
new.notes: NE: §18-1722.01 read whole (Source ends Laws 2021, LB163, § 105), with §76-1416(4): once the governing body decides a property is unsafe or unfit, 'it shall be the duty of such municipality to post the property accordingly and to file a copy of such resolution or other determination in the office of the register of deeds of the county to be recorded'; the duty is the city's, and the row claims no landlord disclosure duty.

note: NE: §18-1722.01 read whole (Source ends Laws 2021, LB163, § 105), with §76-1416(4): once the governing body decides a property is unsafe or unfit, 'it shall be the duty of such municipality to post the property accordingly and to file a copy of such resolution or other determination in the office of the register of deeds of the county to be recorded'; the duty is the city's, and the row claims no landlord disclosure duty.

new.title: Meter Tampering: Who the Utility Presumes Is Responsible
new.bodyText: A Nebraska utility may sue anyone who bypasses or tampers with a meter, or moves or reconnects one without authority, and anyone who benefits from it; on proof the act was willful, it recovers its actual loss or, if that cannot reasonably be calculated, $750, plus its costs (§25-21,276). Two presumptions decide who is blamed. A tenant or occupant who had access to the tampered part of the system and was responsible, directly or indirectly, for paying for the service is presumed to have caused or known of the tampering (§25-21,277(1)). The customer responsible for paying the utility, which may be you if the account is in your name, is presumed to have caused or known of it if the customer controlled access to that part of the system (§25-21,277(2)). Both presumptions can be rebutted. If you keep the account in your name, keep meters in a place you control and document who has access.
new.notes: NE: §§25-21,275 to 25-21,278 read whole (Laws 1983, LB 350; Laws 2002, LB 1105): §25-21,277(2), 'There shall be a rebuttable presumption that a customer at any premises where bypassing, tampering, or unauthorized metering is proven to exist caused or had knowledge of such bypassing, tampering, or unauthorized metering if the customer controlled access to the part of the utility supply system', with 'Customer means the person responsible for payment for utility services for the premises' (§25-21,275(2)); the remedies are 'supplemental and additional' (§25-21,278).

note: NE: §§25-21,275 to 25-21,278 read whole (Laws 1983, LB 350; Laws 2002, LB 1105): §25-21,277(2), 'There shall be a rebuttable presumption that a customer at any premises where bypassing, tampering, or unauthorized metering is proven to exist caused or had knowledge of such bypassing, tampering, or unauthorized metering if the customer controlled access to the part of the utility supply system', with 'Customer means the person responsible for payment for utility services for the premises' (§25-21,275(2)); the remedies are 'supplemental and additional' (§25-21,278).
quote: §25-21,277: '(1) There shall be a rebuttable presumption that a tenant or occupant at any premises where bypassing, tampering, or unauthorized metering is proven to exist caused or had knowledge of such bypassing, tampering, or unauthorized metering if the tenant or occupant (a) had access to the part of the utility supply system on the premises where the bypassing, tampering, or unauthorized metering is proven to exist and (b) was responsible or partially responsible for payment, either directly or indirectly, to the utility or to any other person for utility services to the premises. (2) There shall be a rebuttable presumption that a customer ... caused or had knowledge of such bypassing, tampering, or unauthorized metering if the customer controlled access to the part of the utility supply system'. §25-21,276(2)(b): 'Liquidated damages of seven hundred fifty dollars if the amount of actual damage or loss is not susceptible of reasonable calculation.'

new.title: Protecting Applicant and Tenant Data
new.bodyText: If you keep applicants' or tenants' personal information on a computer, Nebraska's data-security law applies to you whether you are an individual or a company. Personal information means a person's name together with a Social Security number, a driver's license or state ID number, a financial account or card number with the code that opens it, or biometric data, or a user name or email address with its password, where the data is not encrypted or redacted. You must keep reasonable security procedures suited to the information and to the size of your business, including safe disposal (§87-808(1)). If you give that data to an outside service provider, such as a screening company or property-management software, your contract must require the provider to keep reasonable security too (§87-808(2); contracts made or renewed from July 19, 2018). If the data is breached, you must promptly investigate, and if misuse has happened or is reasonably likely, notify the affected Nebraska residents and the Attorney General without unreasonable delay (§87-803). A lease term waiving any of this is void (§87-805). The separate Data Privacy Act applies only to a business that is not a small business under the federal Small Business Act (§87-1103(1)(c)), except for its ban on selling sensitive data without consent (§87-1118).
new.notes: NE: §§87-801 to 87-808 read whole (Laws 2006, LB 876; Laws 2016, LB835; Laws 2018, LB757), with §§87-1103 and 87-1118: §87-808(1) binds 'an individual or a commercial entity that conducts business in Nebraska and owns, licenses, or maintains computerized data that includes personal information about a resident of Nebraska', and (2)(a) requires that it 'shall require by contract that the service provider implement and maintain reasonable security procedures and practices'; enforcement is by the Attorney General, with no private action for §87-808 (§87-806).

note: NE: §§87-801 to 87-808 read whole (Laws 2006, LB 876; Laws 2016, LB835; Laws 2018, LB757), with §§87-1103 and 87-1118: §87-808(1) binds 'an individual or a commercial entity that conducts business in Nebraska and owns, licenses, or maintains computerized data that includes personal information about a resident of Nebraska', and (2)(a) requires that it 'shall require by contract that the service provider implement and maintain reasonable security procedures and practices'; enforcement is by the Attorney General, with no private action for §87-808 (§87-806).
quote: §87-808(1): 'an individual or a commercial entity that conducts business in Nebraska and owns, licenses, or maintains computerized data that includes personal information about a resident of Nebraska shall implement and maintain reasonable security procedures and practices that are appropriate to the nature and sensitivity of the personal information ... including safeguards that protect the personal information when the individual or commercial entity disposes of the personal information.' (2)(a): 'An individual or commercial entity that discloses computerized data that includes personal information about a Nebraska resident to a nonaffiliated, third-party service provider shall require by contract that the service provider implement and maintain reasonable security procedures and practices'.

new.title: If a Licensed Agent Rents the Property for You
new.bodyText: If a real estate licensee, such as a leasing agent or a licensed property manager, offers brokerage services to a prospective tenant who has no written brokerage agreement, the licensee must, at the earliest practicable opportunity during or after the first substantial contact, give the tenant a written copy of the Real Estate Commission's current brokerage disclosure pamphlet and disclose in writing which party the licensee represents (§76-2421(1)). A licensee acting as your agent with an unrepresented tenant must also give the tenant a written statement that the licensee is your agent and not the tenant's, with a list of the tasks the licensee may perform for the tenant, before doing the listed brokerage activities (§76-2421(3)). Each disclosure has a signature block for the tenant to acknowledge receipt; if the tenant will not sign, the licensee notes that on a copy and keeps it (§76-2421(5)). These are the licensee's duties, not yours, but if you use an agent, confirm they are done.
new.notes: NE: §§76-2401 and 76-2421 read whole (Source ends Laws 2011, LB25, § 8), with §76-2417: §76-2421(1) requires the licensee to 'Provide that person with a written copy of the current brokerage disclosure pamphlet which has been prepared and approved by the commission', and the duty runs to a 'seller, landlord, buyer, or tenant'; §76-2421(6) exempts certain entities leasing five or more units, which the row does not need to state for a tenant-facing duty.

note: NE: §§76-2401 and 76-2421 read whole (Source ends Laws 2011, LB25, § 8), with §76-2417: §76-2421(1) requires the licensee to 'Provide that person with a written copy of the current brokerage disclosure pamphlet which has been prepared and approved by the commission', and the duty runs to a 'seller, landlord, buyer, or tenant'; §76-2421(6) exempts certain entities leasing five or more units, which the row does not need to state for a tenant-facing duty.
quote: (1) At the earliest practicable opportunity during or following the first substantial contact with a seller, landlord, buyer, or tenant who has not entered into a written agreement for brokerage services with a designated broker, the licensee who is offering brokerage services to that person or who is providing brokerage services for that property shall: (a) Provide that person with a written copy of the current brokerage disclosure pamphlet which has been prepared and approved by the commission; and (b) Disclose in writing to that person the types of brokerage relationships ... or disclose in writing to that person which party the licensee is representing.

new.title: A Lease Induced by a Deceptive Practice Cannot Be Enforced
new.bodyText: Under Nebraska's Uniform Deceptive Trade Practices Act, if a lessee is induced to sign a lease by a deceptive trade practice listed in §87-302 or by an unconscionable act or practice in a consumer transaction (§87-303.01), the agreement is unenforceable by the lessor, and the lessee may choose to rescind it or keep what was delivered and the benefit of any services without paying for them (§87-303.07). The act's list is written mostly about goods and services, and its text does not settle whether it reaches a residential lease of real property. The cautious course is to assume it does: describe the property, its features, its price and your fees accurately in every advertisement and conversation.
new.notes: NE: §87-303.07 read whole (Laws 1974, LB 327, § 9; Laws 2008, LB781, § 8), with §§87-301, 87-302 (read in the version operative January 1, 2027, Laws 2026, LB838, § 27) and 87-303.01: 'If a buyer or lessee is induced by a violation of section 87-302 or 87-303.01 to enter into a sale or lease, the agreement is unenforceable by the seller or lessor'; §87-302 speaks of 'goods or services' and no definition in §87-301 says whether a real-property lease is covered, so the row states the cautious course.

note: NE: §87-303.07 read whole (Laws 1974, LB 327, § 9; Laws 2008, LB781, § 8), with §§87-301, 87-302 (read in the version operative January 1, 2027, Laws 2026, LB838, § 27) and 87-303.01: 'If a buyer or lessee is induced by a violation of section 87-302 or 87-303.01 to enter into a sale or lease, the agreement is unenforceable by the seller or lessor'; §87-302 speaks of 'goods or services' and no definition in §87-301 says whether a real-property lease is covered, so the row states the cautious course.
quote: If a buyer or lessee is induced by a violation of section 87-302 or 87-303.01 to enter into a sale or lease, the agreement is unenforceable by the seller or lessor and the buyer or lessee, at his or her option, may rescind the agreement or retain the merchandise delivered and the benefit of any services performed without any obligation to pay for them.
